To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the lactate carrier from erythrocyte membrane can be reconstituted in liposomes and that the reconstituted carrier is specific for L-lactate.

we reconstituted the lactate carrier from rabbit and rat erythrocyte membrane into liposomes and found that the rate of pyruvated uptake into these vesicle was inhibited by approx 70% by a-cyano-3-hydroxycimnamic acid.

(1) the lactate carrier from erythrocytes of rats and rabbits is reconstituted with high efficiency into proteoliposomes, and (2) the reconstituted carrier shows a time-dependent uptake of pyruvates and a competitive inhibition by alpha-cyanno-4-hydrocinnamate.

the reconstituted rat and rabbit erythocyte membrane vesicles contain a carrier for L-lactate, which is not present in the bovine erythroctye membrane vesicles.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
reconstituted erythrocyte lactate carrier is a carrier of the L-lac-tate/pyruvate antiporter type, with a low Km for pyruvate and a high Km for lactate.
the reconstituted system is an active L-lactate/pyruvate carrier, which has a high degree of specificity.
the reconstituted system has properties of the lactate carrier of the erythrocyte membrane.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is possible to reconstitute a lactate carrier into artificial membranes from rat and rabbit but not bovine erythroctyes.
the lactate carrier is an electrogenic transporter that is able to exchange H+ and lactate in a 1:1 stoichiometry.
we have developed a reconstitution system that can be used to study the lactate carrier in erythrocytes.
